newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX JGBs, Euroyen up after Japan's reassurance.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX JGBs, Euroyen up after Japan's reassurance.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures rose on Thursday on assurances by Japanese officials that the economy is enroute to a gradual recovery, dealers said.

"The three ministries did not say anything new but what they said was enough to reassure the market Japan is enroute to a recovery at a gradual speed with no inflationary threat," a dealer with a European institution said.
At 1115 GMT, March euroyen was trading around 98.97 against its IMM close at 98.93. December was at 99.165 against its IMM close at 99.140.
JGBs ended higher, with September up 0.28 at 124.86 on 673 lots. Dealers said its next resistance was pegged at 124.95.

Comments by Japan's financial heavyweights -- Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita, Economic Planning Agency Minister Taro Aso and Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka -- reassured the market that efforts are being made to ensure an economic recovery, dealers said.
The comments made at an annual bankers convention also helped erase lingering fears of near term rate hikes.
Matsushita said the slowdown in Japan's economy is temporary and the BOJ's monetary policy will continue to aim at strengthening a recovery.
A continued accommodative monetary stance by the BOJ reinforced belief in a steady Japanese rate at least during summer, dealers said. Most expect a rate hike in the fourth quarter.
Eurodollar futures held steady after the Federal Open Market Committe (FOMC) left rates unchanged. March ended at 93.875 against its IMM close at 93.88.
"Activity was quiet ahead of the long weekend in the U.S. Traders were cautious ahead of the June nonfarm payroll data due out tonight," a dealer with a Japanese bank said.
According to a Reuters poll, U.S. employment in June is expected to have risen 222,000 after a 138,000 gain in May. But many are forecasting as high as 300,000 gain.
